phase: Phase 8 final record (supersedes Phase 8 and 8b figures where noted)

configuration.think: 'low' where the model declares the thinking capability, omitted otherwise
configuration.why: context 32768 removes truncation; max_iters 40 removes interruption; untrimmed because trimming doubled the schema-error rate; think='low' measured best of the settings tried

qwen3.5:9b.hardware_verdict: cannot hold the tool surface on GPU: the schema floor with EVERY description deleted is 2690 tokens, which exceeds its 2048-token GPU-resident context by 642

schema_token_cost.trim_verdict: REVERTED — saved 1684 tokens but raised schema-invalid 16.4% -> 31.8% at matched settings
schema_token_cost.other_consumer: benchmark/mcp_client.py forwards tool.description to models; 6 recorded run sets in benchmark/runs/ would become non-comparable, so descriptions were never edited at source

iteration_cap.verdict: the cap was interruption, not non-termination; at 40 no run is cut off

thinking.docs: think is 'a boolean or a thinking level (low, medium, high, max)'; no default stated
thinking.verdict: levels are non-monotonic and overlap heavily; only the boolean is a reliable control, but think='low' measured best on task and is the chosen setting

open_questions: Neither model reached the ceiling reasoning in 10 runs: both say 'moderate' but neither explains that moderate IS the maximum for a balanced event.
qwen3.5:9b's reasoning remains effectively unmeasured: it answered 11/30, and 5 runs hit transport errors (1 timeout, 4 HTTP 500) under CPU spill.
The 7b's schema-invalid rate rose 4.4% -> 13.4% when allowed longer chains; whether that is chain length or context is untested.
think='medium'/'high' were characterised only on a trivial prompt, not on task.
